reason: A canaliculate or channeled leaf base is a groove. The examples fit.
A disc can be bilobed, and the examples describe the disc itself.
Sticky or viscid seeds or seed surfaces are real. One example is about sticky hairs on the seed, but the pair is still fine.
The text 'drop-shaped' was split into 'dro p', and 'drooping' was matched from it. This is a wrong reading, and a drop shape is not drooping.
The coriaceous part is the tunics or outer coats, not the bulb. A rule would need to say whether tunic quality goes to the bulb or to a tunic part.
Subapical or subterminal position of a bracteole is a real position.
A plicate corolla is real. In some examples only the sinuses are plicate, but the pair is meaningful.

'Variable in size or colour' says the flower varies in a named feature. It is not a quality of the flower itself. A rule would need to attach variability to the named feature (colour, size) and not to the flower.
Subtriangular stipules are normal.
Tubers are described as thick. The examples are thickness measurements, so the pair is fine.
Tricuspidate or tridentate bract apices are real.
Small outer involucral bracts are correct.
Foveolate or pitted spore surfaces are standard in pteridophyte descriptions.
'Styles 2–3 × stylopodium' is a length ratio to another part, not a count. The amount reading is wrong. A ratio rule is needed.
Lip size, such as equal or larger than other parts, is a real size statement.
Lenticel diameter is correct.
Veins can be pubescent. Some examples describe the leaf surface, but the pair is meaningful.
An undulate margin is standard.
Short buds are meaningful. One example is noisy (inflorescence and bud), but the pair is fine.
A calyptra can be lobed at the base. This is the standard moss description.
Lobed organs (leaf, corolla, calyx) are common. The depth is a separate matter.
'Angled' means with edges (a cross-section shape). It is not bent. The pair comes from a wrong reading.
Uniform sporophylls are meaningful, meaning all of one form.
A narrow hypanthium or floral tube is correct.
A lemma awn count (1-awned, 3-awned) is a real count, and the awn is the bearer.
Acute disc lobes or apex are fine.
Erect disc lobes or margins are fine.
A fragile rachilla is a standard grass character.
Small or minute petiolules are correct.
The thickness is of the cell wall, not of the cell. A rule would need a cell wall part, or it should map 'walls thick' to that part.
Hair length is correct.
'Uniform in size' says the leaves are alike, which is variation among leaves. A rule would need to tell uniformity between organs from a quality of one leaf.
Coriaceous cataphylls or scale leaves are correct.
Elongate shoot systems or innovations are fine.
Aporose means without pores, which is imperforate, for moss cells and surfaces.
A vertical embryo axis is a real character. The quality is about the embryo's orientation.
A unilateral disc is a real character, with the disc on one side.
A central hilum is correct.
Pyramidal or tetrahedral seeds are real.
French 'velu' means hairy or villous. It is not velvety (velutinous), so the reading is wrong. Map it to the villous or hairy term.
Pubescent or pubérulent pedicels are correct.
Reticulate venation pattern of secondary veins is meaningful.
Axis diameter is correct.
'Strié' means striate or streaked, and 'banded' is not the same. A rule would need to map 'strié' to the striate term and keep banded for bands.
Nectary length is correct.
Straight pappus bristles are correct.
Pollen sacs in one row or in pairs are an arrangement pattern. Some examples show a different part (crown), but the pair is fine.
The text 'fruits à galles' says the host organ has galls. The gall itself is not 'present'. Presence belongs on the host organ.
Chartaceous (papery) is close to papyraceous but not always the same. A rule would need to say whether the two are treated as one texture term.
A filiform apex of a trichome or scale is correct.
Paraphysis width is correct.
Deciduous or caducous scales and trichomes are real.
A circular staminal disc is correct.
A straight capsule mouth is unclear, since it could refer to the mouth line or to the peristome. A rule would need to say which feature is meant.
'2.5–4.5 cm broad' is a measured width. It belongs to a width quality, not to the 'broad' shape term.
Filamentose sheaths means the sheaths break into fibres. It is a state of the sheaths, not of the scale leaf as a whole, and a rule is needed for fibrous breakdown.
A striate perigynium (many-nerved) is a standard sedge character.
Attenuate lodicules are meaningful.
An obtuse fertile lemma is correct.
Rose-coloured bracts or bract tips are correct.
